sources.title: Growth years and post-harvest processing methods have critical roles on the contents of medicinal active ingredients of Scutellaria baicalensis.
sources.authors: Bai C; Yang J; Cao B; Xue Y; Gao P; Liang H; Li G
quotes: Baikal Skullcap (Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi) is a perennial herb in the Lamiaceae family and its dried root is used as a famous traditional Chinese medicine (TCM).

The contents of eight active ingredients (baicalin, wogonoside, baicalein, wogonin, scutellarin, scutellarein, apigenin, and chrysin) in roots of S. baicalensis of different growth years (ranging from 1 year to 15 years) were estimated using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and further analyzed to determine the optimal harvest period.

The results showed that the best harvesting period for S. baicalensis should be determined as 2-3 years based on comprehensive evaluation of active ingredient content, annual yield increment, and land use efficiency. The contents of active ingredients including baicalin, wogonoside, baicalein, and wogonin in cortex were significantly higher than those in stele (P ≤ 0.05).

For the effects of different processing treatments, the contents of four main active ingredients (baicalin, wogonoside, baicalein, and wogonin) under drying (D) and cutting-drying (C-D) treatments were significantly higher than those of the other four treatments (P ≤ 0.05).

Assay | Baicalin: ≥9.0 % | Baicalin: ≥10.0 % | ≥10.0 % (total of Baicalin, baicalein and wogonin) | Baicalin: ≥9.0 % | ≥11.0 % (total of Baicalin and wogonin-7-O-glucuronide);
≥3.50 % (total of Baicalin and wogonin) | Baicalin: ≥9.0 % | Baicalin: ≥8.0 %

claims.claim: In HPLC screening of 38 samples from seven main cultivated areas, baicalin, wogonoside and baicalein were the three main flavonoids with the highest contents, and flavonoid content differed markedly between cultivation regions.
claims.quote: baicalin, wogonoside, and baicalein were the three main flavonoids with the highest contents in Radix Scutellaria. The content of flavonoids in different cultivated areas was very different, which had significant regionality and was closely related to the natural conditions of various places.

claims.claim: Growth year determines quality: the best harvesting period for S. baicalensis is 2-3 years, and the root cortex contains significantly more baicalin, wogonoside, baicalein and wogonin than the stele.
claims.quote: The results showed that the best harvesting period for S. baicalensis should be determined as 2-3 years based on comprehensive evaluation of active ingredient content, annual yield increment, and land use efficiency. The contents of active ingredients including baicalin, wogonoside, baicalein, and wogonin in cortex were significantly higher than those in stele (P ≤ 0.05).

claims.claim: Traditional wine-processing (pao zhi) changes the dissolution of compounds from Radix Scutellariae by altering the pore structure of the material.
claims.quote: The data indicated that wine-processing would affect the dissolution of compounds by changing the pore structure of RS.

claims.claim: Baicalin shows a distinct pharmacokinetic profile including gastrointestinal hydrolysis, enterohepatic recycling, carrier-mediated transport and complicated metabolism.
claims.quote: Baicalin displays a distinct pharmacokinetic profile including gastrointestinal hydrolysis, enterohepatic recycling, carrier-mediated transport, and complicated metabolism.

claims.claim: Probiotic fermentation markedly modifies the bioactive components of S. baicalensis (flavonoids such as baicalin, baicalein and wogonin), augmenting its medicinal potency.
claims.quote: Evidence suggests that probiotic fermentation markedly modifies the bioactive components of Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, thereby augmenting its medicinal potency.

claims.claim: S. baicalensis has been officially listed in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia for a long time, and chromatographic fingerprints combined with quantitative multi-component analysis can be used for its quality evaluation.
claims.quote: _Scutellaria baicalensis_ Georgi (Labiatae) is one commonly used herbal medicine in China and other East Asian countries, and it has been officially listed in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia for a long time [\[19\]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7125791/#bib19).

claims.claim: Four highly variable chloroplast genome regions (matK-rps16, ndhC-trnV-UAC, psbE-petL, rps16-trnQ-UUG) are candidate DNA barcode markers for differentiating S. baicalensis from its adulterants; substitution with comparable species occurs in local markets.
claims.quote: Four highly variable regions (matK-rps16, ndhC-trnV-UAC, psbE-petL, and rps16-trnQ-UUG) may function as potential molecular markers for differentiating S. baicalensis from its adulterants.

claims.claim: Commercial S. baicalensis extracts vary widely: of 10 commercial extracts analyzed, 4 contained no baicalin at all, and growth-inhibition potency varied more than 11-fold between products.
claims.quote: However, significant product-to-product and batch-to-batch variation of these marker components was observed with 4 products containing no baicalin at all and baicalein concentration ranging from 0 to 52.3 g/mg. The 50% growth inhibition concentration of the extracts ranged from 0.18 to 2.0 mg/ml, more than an 11-fold variation. PGE2 levels varied from 19.5 to 111.1 pg/106 cells, more than a 5.7-fold difference.

claims.claim: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 85 healthy adults taking 240 mg/day of a Scutellaria baicalensis stem extract combined with Acacia catechu for four weeks showed enhanced cognitive function overall but without significant advantage over placebo, and the supplement was well tolerated.
claims.quote: Four-week daily TP supplementation significantly enhanced cognitive function without difference from placebo.
